devices.name: Symploce
devices.definition: Anaphora and epistrophe together — clauses that share both their opening and closing words.

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

occurrences.note: " Babylon is fallen, is fallen ": to emphasize the certainty and the greatness of the fall of that great city, and the completeness of its final overthrow

devices.name: Hermeneia
devices.definition: Interpretation: a plain restatement added at once to explain a figure just used.

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

devices.name: Syllogismus
devices.definition: The conclusion is left unstated, so the hearer is made to draw it — an unspoken inference.

devices.name: Allegory
devices.definition: An extended metaphor — a whole passage whose surface story stands throughout for a deeper meaning.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Asyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions omitted between items in a series, producing a rapid, piled-up effect.

devices.name: Ecphonesis
devices.definition: An outcry of feeling — a sudden exclamation breaking from strong emotion (“O the depth!”).

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Hyperbaton
devices.definition: Words wrenched out of their natural order, throwing weight onto the displaced word.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

occurrences.note: Matt, xi, II. — "Born of women "; i.e., born by natural process

devices.name: Tapeinosis
devices.definition: Deliberate understatement — belittling a thing to magnify it, or lessening to increase the effect.

devices.name: Ampliatio
devices.definition: An old name kept for a person or thing after the reason for it has passed (“the blind man” once healed).

occurrences.note: former the Saviour is so called by the angels while still an infant

devices.name: Anabasis
devices.definition: A gradual ascent — a series that mounts, clause by clause, to a high point.

occurrences.note: " Ah sinful nation, A people laden with iniquity, A seed of evildoers, Children that are corrupters."

devices.name: Anadiplosis
devices.definition: The word ending one clause is repeated to begin the next, linking them.

devices.name: Antonomasia
devices.definition: A proper name replaced by a descriptive title, or a title by a proper name (“the Son of man”).

devices.name: Apodioxis
devices.definition: Indignant rejection of an argument or suggestion as abhorrent (“Get behind me, Satan”).

devices.name: Catabasis
devices.definition: A gradual descent — a series that steps down, clause by clause, to a low point (opposite of climax).

devices.name: Epanodos
devices.definition: Repetition of the chief words of a sentence in inverse order, to expound them.

devices.name: Epitrechon
devices.definition: A clause “running through” — dropped in parenthetically between others.

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

devices.name: Maledictio
devices.definition: An imprecation or pronouncement of woe (“Woe to you…”).

devices.name: Merism
devices.definition: Naming the parts, or the two extremes, to mean the whole — “heaven and earth,” “your going out and your coming in.”

devices.name: Metalepsis
devices.definition: A double metonymy: one word stands for a second, which itself stands for a third.

devices.name: Metaphor
devices.definition: An implied comparison that calls one thing another (“A is B”), without “like” or “as.”

devices.name: Palinodia
devices.definition: A concession — granting a point for argument's sake before answering it.

devices.name: Paregmenon
devices.definition: Words from the same root set near one another (a figure of derivation).

devices.name: Syncrisis
devices.definition: Reconciling or comparing opposites, setting contraries together to make a point.

occurrences.note: "And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land."

devices.name: Zeugma
devices.definition: One verb made to govern two objects though it strictly fits only one; the second borrows it.
